<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

{"body_md": "## Problem
Garage estimate documents are automatically placed in the wrong category, forcing manual correction. This leads to missed evidence and delays because critical information is overlooked during claims processing.

## Who is affected
- Five accounts have reported this issue, representing a total ARR of £4,290,000 [i:0b669b812359487f][i:0fc6cb6155656fe2][i:6401b85f53f8e56b][i:6f60a28973334f3b].
- The problem has been raised by customers across three routes: support, account management, and onboarding [i:0b669b812359487f][i:0fc6cb6155656fe2][i:6401b85f53f8e56b].
- One account, Marrowgate Commercial, has a renewal date of 2026-12-12 [i:6401b85f53f8e56b][i:766f9ca2be319649].

## Evidence
- There have been 13 mentions of this problem from the five accounts [i:0b669b812359487f][i:0fc6cb6155656fe2][i:6401b85f53f8e56b].
- Eight mentions came via the support route [i:0b669b812359487f][i:27425ffc5bea7e8a][i:35bc60912c19d67e][i:5109cfcbf29475a5][i:6f60a28973334f3b][i:71622a189d0b930d][i:8621fe0ded65ffe4][i:a3f2a53f98cd8130].
- Two mentions came via the account management route [i:0fc6cb6155656fe2][i:1d02c338591f1b06].
- Three mentions came via the onboarding route [i:6401b85f53f8e56b][i:766f9ca2be319649][i:a918397cecacd89d].
- Saltmarsh Specialty, with an ARR of £740,000, has stated that garage estimates keep landing in correspondence, forcing manual recategorisation and risking missed evidence [i:0b669b812359487f]. They also report that handlers are spending too much time fixing incorrect file type assignments, which impacts claim accuracy [i:35bc60912c19d67e][i:71622a189d0b930d].
- Linnet House Insurance, with an ARR of £360,000, reports that every time a garage estimate gets dumped into correspondence, someone has to manually fix it, and evidence can be overlooked [i:0fc6cb6155656fe2]. They have reiterated this issue via support, stating it risks missing critical evidence [i:27425ffc5bea7e8a][i:5109cfcbf29475a5].
- Thistlecombe Mutual, with an ARR of £980,000, has mentioned the document upload system assigning the wrong category, putting repair quotes under correspondence [i:1d02c338591f1b06].
- Marrowgate Commercial, with an ARR of £1,600,000, reported during onboarding that garage estimates land under Correspondence, causing handlers to manually re-categorise everything [i:6401b85f53f8e56b]. They later noted this manual work risks things slipping through the cracks and causes delays in handling claims properly [i:766f9ca2be319649][i:a918397cecacd89d].
- Brackwater Homecover, with an ARR of £610,000, states that when they upload a garage estimate, it lands in correspondence, which is a wrong document category causing handlers to miss key evidence and delay claims resolution [i:6f60a28973334f3b][i:a3f2a53f98cd8130].

## Why now
- One renewal has occurred in the last 90 days [i:0b669b812359487f][i:0fc6cb6155656fe2][i:6401b85f53f8e56b].
- The most recent mentions from customers occurred in October 2026, indicating the problem is current and actively causing operational pain [i:0b669b812359487f][i:27425ffc5bea7e8a][i:6f60a28973334f3b][i:a3f2a53f98cd8130].
- Marrowgate Commercial, a key account with an ARR of £1,600,000, has a renewal date of 2026-12-12, and they have recently highlighted this issue as causing delays [i:6401b85f53f8e56b][i:a918397cecacd89d].", "citations": ["0b669b812359487f", "0fc6cb6155656fe2", "6401b85f53f8e56b", "6f60a28973334f3b", "27425ffc5bea7e8a", "5109cfcbf29475a5", "35bc60912c19d67e", "71622a189d0b930d", "8621fe0ded65ffe4", "1d02c338591f1b06", "766f9ca2be319649", "a918397cecacd89d", "a3f2a53f98cd8130"]}
